## Mutant validation

A mutant is *killed as intended* when its intended invariant FAILs in at least one run of one of its intended scenarios without any infrastructure error.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `m1_stale_backfill` | `S1_ACKED_DURABLE` | 3/3 | yes | S7_LINEARIZABLE | 10/10 pass |
| `m2_nonatomic_dual_write` | `S3_REPR_AGREEMENT` | 3/3 | yes | S1_ACKED_DURABLE, S7_LINEARIZABLE | 10/10 pass |
| `m3_retry_duplicates` | `S4_NO_DUPLICATION` | 3/3 | yes | S7_LINEARIZABLE | 10/10 pass |
| `m4_premature_contract` | `C1_COMPATIBILITY` | 3/3 | yes | - | 9/10 pass (fails CT08) |
| `m5_backfill_skips_row` | `R4_TERMINAL_STATE` | 6/6 | yes | R1_INTERRUPTED_RESUMES, R3_BACKFILL_RETRY_SAFE | 9/10 pass (fails CT07) |
| `m6_float_cents` | `S2_EXACT_CENTS` | 3/3 | yes | S7_LINEARIZABLE | 9/10 pass (fails CT06) |

## Conventional suite (per test)

| Implementation | CT01 | CT02 | CT03 | CT04 | CT05 | CT06 | CT07 | CT08 | CT09 | CT10 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ref_a_trigger` | pass | pass | pass | pass | pass | pass | pass | pass | pass | pass |
| `ref_b_dualwrite` | pass | pass | pass | pass | pass | pass | pass | pass | pass | pass |
| `m1_stale_backfill` | pass | pass | pass | pass | pass | pass | pass | pass | pass | pass |
| `m2_nonatomic_dual_write` | pass | pass | pass | pass | pass | pass | pass | pass | pass | pass |
| `m3_retry_duplicates` | pass | pass | pass | pass | pass | pass | pass | pass | pass | pass |
| `m4_premature_contract` | pass | pass | pass | pass | pass | pass | pass | FAIL | pass | pass |
| `m5_backfill_skips_row` | pass | pass | pass | pass | pass | pass | FAIL | pass | pass | pass |
| `m6_float_cents` | pass | pass | pass | pass | pass | FAIL | pass | pass | pass | pass |
| `m7_assumes_backfilled` | pass | pass | pass | pass | pass | pass | pass | pass | pass | pass |
| `m8_skip_reconcile` | pass | pass | pass | pass | pass | pass | pass | pass | pass | pass |

Tests: CT01 = v1 create then read returns the same total; CT02 = v1 add_charge returns and persists the new total; CT03 = v1 add_charge with a repeated key is applied once; CT04 = unknown orders are reported as not_found; CT05 = after expand, v2 reads legacy rows correctly; CT06 = v2 create / set_total / add_charge / read; CT07 = full sequential migration preserves every value; CT08 = finalize is refused while a v1 instance is registered; CT09 = v2 operates normally after contract; CT10 = invalid amounts are rejected without side effects

## Limitations of these results

- Interleavings are explored at SQL-statement granularity under a single-threaded controller; behaviour that depends on true parallel execution inside PostgreSQL (e.g. simultaneous lock acquisition) is not explored.
- Each schedule is either scripted or drawn from a seeded random policy; there is no systematic or coverage-guided search of the interleaving space.
- The linearizability oracle may place an uncertain operation's effect anywhere in the union of its attempts' windows, which is slightly more permissive than the real constraint.
- Relaxation-based diagnoses (S1/S2/S4/S6) mean 'consistent with', not proof of root cause.
- Determinism assumes the same PostgreSQL version and configuration; deadlock-victim choice and other timing-dependent server behaviour are not controlled.
- Results cover reference implementations and hand-written mutants only. No external AI agent has been evaluated.
